children: By Satoshi Sugiyama

Japan's Nikkei share average slipped more than 1% on Tuesday, tracking a selloff on Wall Street, as investors remained on the sidelines ahead of Nvidia's third-quarter earnings and Anthropic's initial public offering.
The Nikkei 225 Index
was down 1.1% at 58,998.39, as of 0149 GMT. The broader Topix
AI- and chip-related shares led declines, with Advantest
falling 5.07%, Kioxia Holdings
shedding 4.58% and SoftBank Group
losing 4.1%.

"Caution ahead of Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO is... expected to keep investors from buying aggressively, adding to pressure on stocks," Monex Securities analyst Yoshitaka Araya said in a report.
US megacap and AI-linked stocks, including Nvidia
, fell overnight on concerns over the outlook for the sector after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation last week.

Enthusiasm for AI stocks also eased after the US government announced efforts to further tighten China's access to advanced AI chips from firms such as Nvidia ahead of a high-stakes meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
In Tokyo, energy explorer stocks (.IMING.T) fell 3.7% as oil prices slipped on expectations of supply surplus, weighing on the sector, while lower US Treasury yields pushed banking shares
down 3.07%.
The market breadth was largely negative, with 62 advancers on the Nikkei 225 against 162 decliners and 1 unchanged.
The largest losers by percentage in the index were Ibiden
, down 5.44%, followed by Furukawa Electric
, trading 5.35% lower, and  Mitsui Kinzoku
, which lost 4.43%.
The largest percentage gainers in the index were Recruit Holdings
, up 3.72%, followed by Credit Saison
, trading 2.59% higher, and Yokogawa Electric Corporation
, which gained 2.32%.
